newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks governments to train, modernise workforces.
newsitem.headline: EU asks governments to train, modernise workforces.

text.p: European Union labour and economy ministers adopted a joint report on Monday asking EU governments and industry to help boost employment by modernising and educating their workforces.
"The achievement of a productive and flexible economy depends on the workforce being able to respond to the skills needs of the labour market," it said.

The ministers, who prepared the report for the EU summit in Dublin later this month, said governments should reinforce their training schemes, giving priority to bringing young people into the job market and preventing the jobless from drifting into long-term unemployment.
They said governments, industry and labour unions also needed to do more to make workers more responsive to economic changes, for example by promoting increased mobility.

"There is a strong need for a forceful human resources policy to meet the skills requirement of the new organisation of working life, driven by the new information and communication technologies," they said.
Irish Employment Minister Eithne Fitzgerald, who chaired the meeting of labour ministers, said the report was optimistic about prospects for boosting economic growth and jobs in Europe.

"The fundamental economic conditions are better than they were 10 years ago, when Europe created 10 million extra jobs," she told a news conference. "So we're saying it's time now for business to invest in Europe's future."

The report said that EU wage and price increases were low, interest rates were converging towards a lower level, exchange rates in most countries were broadly stable and the profitability of job-creating investments had improved.
